newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas eases ahead of milder weather.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas eases ahead of milder weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices drifted lower Tuesday as forecasts called for milder weather in western Canada, market sources said.
Temperatures in Calgary were forecast to rise Wednesday and Thursday to highs of 47 and 57 degrees Fahrenheit, respectively, Weather Services Corp said.
As a result, spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked about four cents lower at C$1.58-1.59 per gigajoule (GJ).
Also putting pressure on the market was a drop in field receipts into Empress, which was backing some gas back into Alberta.

"Storage went in really hard over the weekend, and heating demand hasn't picked up that much despite the snow," one Calgary-based trader said, adding he expected prices to remain lower over the next couple of days.
June AECO was quoted at C$1.63-1.64 per GJ.
At Sumas, Wash., prices slipped one cent to $1.28-1.29 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) due to a return of more seasonable weather to the Northwest.
At Niagara, prices fell by about three cents to $2.39-2.40 per mmBtu.
In Toronto, temperatures were forecast to climb to a high of 57 and 63 degrees F on Wednesday and Thursday, respectively. Lows were expected to remain in the high-30s F, WSC said.
